decisions.reason: As a close-to-core supplement line with several variants, it likely generated enough learning and sales to stay near aspiration, and a large expanding firm can keep it in the portfolio.
This consumer-health extension had a clear launch push and still fits the firm's portfolio-broadening strategy, so unless performance clearly disappointed it would usually be retained.

Because it was less prominently supported and has had ample time to prove itself, management would be more likely to judge it below aspiration and reallocate resources to stronger lines or new projects.
The launch-period problem signal in a price-pressured generic market makes it likely that results stayed below aspiration, prompting withdrawal in favor of safer products and development work.

Despite being a newer and somewhat more distant product, it had dedicated presentation and fits the firm's consumer-health expansion, so the firm would likely continue it while performance evidence accumulates.
